inj.note: Fagnano -- who was inactive for Sunday's contest as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback -- ended up being pressed into action after starter Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) left the game early. The undrafted rookie out of UConn ended up directing the offense for most of the afternoon, completing just 10 of 21 pass attempts for 91 yards and an interception while adding three yards on three carries and losing a fumble in what was his NFL debut. Fagnano was spotted clutching his knee in discomfort after Bills defender Ed Oliver took him down on a play in which he was ultimately flagged for roughing the passer, but the quarterback was able to remain in the game. With Jackson ticketed for injured reserve and Huntley at risk of sitting out the game against Jacksonville, Fagnano could be in line to start Thursday, provided he's not too banged up to handle the assignment.
